1.explanation:
1. We import and render the Carbon UI Shell Header and the SkipToContent component so that the “Skip to main content” link is always in the DOM with its default color styling (background #0f62fe / text #ffffff).

2. We add a HeaderNavigation with both a HeaderMenuItem and a HeaderMenu + sub-items.  In a wide viewport these items are correctly nested under `<ul role=\"menubar\">`, but when you shrink the viewport past Carbon’s navigation-collapse breakpoint, the same links are placed in a side panel `<ul>` that has no ARIA role.  Each link maintains its `role="menuitem"` (or the `<a>` gets that role), triggering the DAP violation “role menuitem is not contained in a parent with role menu, menubar or group.”

3. To reproduce: run the app, open Chrome DevTools → DAP tab, first scan in wide view (you’ll see the contrast error on SkipToContent), then resize under the collapse width, open the side panel, re-scan (you’ll see the missing parent role error on the menu items).  This matches the two violations shown in the bug report screenshot.
1.bug_scenario:
When you render the Carbon React UI Shell “Header Base w/Navigation” (or Header Base w/Navigation + Actions) you will see two DAP violations when you run the IBM DAP Chrome extension:

1. Contrast failure on the permanently visible “Skip to main content” link.  The link is styled with background #0f62fe and text #ffffff, but DAP reports a contrast ratio of 1.91:1 which does not meet WCAG AA for 14px/400 weight text.

2. When you narrow the viewport below the navigation-wrap breakpoint, the navigation collapses into a side panel and the links are rendered in an un-labeled `<ul>`.  In that collapsed panel the `<a>` tags (or `<li>`) get a `role="menuitem"` but their parent `<ul>` has no ARIA role of `menu`, `menubar` or `group`, so DAP complains that “An element with WAI-ARIA role menuitem is not contained in or owned by an element with one of the following WAI-ARIA roles: group, menu, menubar.”
